XXII.}}</noinclude>the violence of the people. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=36}}† For the multitude of the people folovved, crying, Avvay vvith him. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=37}}† And vvhen Paul began to be brought into the castel, he saith to the Tribune, Is it lavvful for me to speake some thing to thee? Vvho said, Canst thou speake Greeke? {{verse|chapter=21|verse=38}}† Art not thou the Ægyptian that before these daies did raise a tumult, and didst lead forth into the desert foure thousand men that vvere murderers? {{verse|chapter=21|verse=39}}† And Paul said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 22, 3.''}}* I am a man truely a Iewe of Tarsus, a citizen not of an obscure citie of Cilicia. And I desire thee, permit me to speake to the people. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=40}}† And vvhen he had permitted him, Paul standing on the staiers, beckened with his hand to the people. and great silence being made, he spake vnto them in the Hebrevv tongue, saying.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XXI.}}}}

''9. Virgins.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Virgins.}}S. Luke noteth specially that his daughters vvere Virgins; meaning (no doubt) that they vvere of the state, profession, or purpose of perpetual virginitie, not only that they vvere yong maides vnmaried: and that they vvere the rather for that, endued with the gift of prophecie, as S. Hierom saith ''li. 1 adu. Iouin. c. 24. See Oecum. c. 29 in hunc locum''.

''24. Keeping the Law.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Auoiding of scādal in things not vnlawful.}}Al the obseruations of the Law were now in them selues dead and vnprofitable, yet til further propagation of the Gospel, they were not damnable to the keepers, nor offensiue to God, but might be obserued euen of the Christian Iewes. and for feare of scandalizing the weake of that nation, newly conuerted or prone to receiue the faith, the Apostles by Gods suggestion did thinke it good to obserue them as occasion required.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXII.}}}}}}

{{c|''Being licensed by the Tribune to speake to the people, he sheweth them that he vvas once as earnest on that side as they now be: 6 and how strange and miraculous his conuersion vvas. 17 They heare him quietly, vntil he began to make mention of a vision that sent him avvay from them to the Gentils. 22 Then they crie out vpon him so, 23 that for their crying the Tribune commaundeth him to be scourged. 25 Which yet by his wisedom he escapeth.''}} {{dropinitial|M|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial M, a grotesque mask.png|imgsize=225px|fl={{verse|chapter=22|verse=1}}}}EN brethren and fathers, heare vvhat account I doe render novv vnto you. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=2}}† (And vvhen they had heard that he spake to them in the Hebrevv tongue, they did the more keepe silence. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=3}}† And he saith,) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 21, 39.''}}* I am a man a Iewe, borne at Tarsus in Cilicia, but brought vp in this citie, at the feete of Gamaliel instructed according to the veritie<noinclude>{{rh|||of}}</noinclude>
